sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Television is a major source of air pollution. (ii) Trees help keep air fresh and pure. (iii) Garbage should not be burnt. (iv) CNG increases pollution.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – CNG is a cleaner fuel and reduces pollution.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Wind decreases the amount of dust particles in the air. (ii) Tall chimneys fitted with filters help to reduce air pollution. (iii) Locating factories near residential areas reduces air pollution. (iv) A tall chimney on a chulha decreases air pollution at home.
questions.answer: (i) False – wind increases dust in the air. (ii) True. (iii) False – factories should be far from residential areas. (iv) True.

questions.q: Match the columns: (i) Composting (ii) Spitting (iii) Soil (iv) Burning of refuse; (a) becomes polluted by waste from factories (b) can be used as manure (c) germs remain after the sputum dries (d) banned in metropolitan cities.
Match the source with the type of pollution: (i) Vehicles (ii) Washing clothes in a river (iii) Loudspeaker (iv) Garbage on roadside; (a) water (b) noise (c) air (d) soil.

Fill in the blanks: (i) The substances that cause pollution are called ______. (ii) A furnace in which garbage is burnt is an ______. (iii) The mark put on environment-friendly goods is the ______. (iv) Water that is safe has no taste, smell, colour or ______.

State True or False: (i) Loud noise can damage hearing. (ii) Burning of refuse is banned in metros. (iii) Fish die in polluted water because less oxygen is available. (iv) Latrines should be built close to water sources.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – they should be far from water sources.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Suggest four efforts that people can make to reduce noise pollution in their society.
questions.answer: Play radio and TV at low volume; avoid loudspeakers; blow vehicle horns only when necessary; fit silencers in vehicles; talk in low tones; build factories and airports away from residential areas (any four).

questions.q: Identify any four reasons for increase in land (soil) pollution in cities.
questions.answer: Improper disposal of garbage; wastes from factories (chemicals and metals); excess use of pesticides and fertilisers; open defecation and urination; spitting; plastic and non-biodegradable products.

questions.q: Give any four suggestions to control air pollution in your area.
questions.answer: Use smokeless fuels like biogas or a solar cooker; keep vehicles in good order and use CNG or unleaded petrol; do not burn garbage; plant trees; make roads pucca; locate factories away from houses and fit chimney filters.

questions.q: Identify four ways people are responsible for causing noise pollution.
questions.answer: Playing radio, TV or music at full volume; use of loudspeakers; unnecessary honking; vehicles without silencers; operating noisy machines and generators near houses.

or.q: What are four possible reasons for increase in polluted air in our cities?
or.answer: Increase in vehicles and their exhaust; smoke from factories and power stations; burning of garbage and household fuel; bursting of crackers; construction dust and cutting of trees.

questions.q: Give any four suggestions for safe garbage disposal in your area.
questions.answer: Collect garbage in a covered bin; dump in covered pits outside the city; use sanitary landfills; compost garden waste; incinerate in a furnace; never burn it in the open or throw it into water.

questions.q: How do oil spills in water bodies affect plant and animal life?
questions.answer: Oil spreads over a large area of the sea and cuts off oxygen, so water plants and animals such as fish die for lack of oxygen and the plant and animal life is badly affected.

questions.q: Write two measures to control soil pollution.
questions.answer: Proper disposal of garbage in covered bins and landfills; use of sanitary latrines; limited use of pesticides and fertilisers; use of Eco-mark products (any two).

questions.q: Define pollution and pollutant.
questions.answer: Pollution is the addition of any substance to the environment in excess of what is normally present, making it impure. The substances that cause it, such as dust, garbage, chemicals and industrial waste, are pollutants.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Identify any six reasons for the increase in noise pollution in the world.
questions.answer: Increase in the number of vehicles and their horns; trains and aircraft; loudspeakers at festivals, weddings and political events; radio, TV and music systems played loud; growth of industries and machines; construction work and generators; crowded cities and growing population; factories and airports built near residential areas.

or.q: Suggest any six ways air can be prevented from getting polluted.
or.answer: Use smokeless chulha or biogas or solar cooker; chimney filters in factories; factories far from residential areas; fit vehicles with devices and use CNG or unleaded petrol; do not burn garbage; make roads pucca; plant and care for trees; grow crops all year to prevent soil erosion.

questions.q: Make the villagers aware of the ill effects of air pollution on health. Suggest four ways to control it.
questions.answer: Air pollution causes eye infections, allergies, bronchitis and asthma, and makes breathing difficult; smoke from chullahs affects the eyes and lungs. Control: use a smokeless chulha with a chimney or biogas, use a solar cooker, do not burn garbage and crop residue, plant trees, keep vehicles in good condition.

or.q: Make your friends aware of the ill effects of water pollution on health. Suggest four ways to control it.
or.answer: Polluted water causes cholera, typhoid, diarrhoea, dysentery and hepatitis, and skin diseases and allergies. Control: do not let untreated sewage or factory waste into water; use latrines and keep them away from water sources; do not wash clothes or bathe animals in the source; keep water in clean covered containers and use a long-handled ladle.

questions.q: Briefly describe any three methods of garbage disposal.
questions.answer: Landfill: low-lying land outside the city is used and garbage is dumped daily and covered. Composting: garden garbage is put in a pit and covered with ash and leaves; the lower layers turn into manure. Incineration: garbage is burnt in a furnace; it is sterile and safe and leaves a small heap of ash but is expensive. (Burning in the open causes smoke and is banned in metros.)

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the sources, effects and any three ways of controlling air pollution.
questions.answer: Sources: combustion of fuel, vehicle exhaust, factory smoke, crackers, pesticide spray, solvents, and natural sources like forest fires and volcanoes. Effects: eye infections, bronchitis, asthma and allergies, poor visibility and smog, less food production in plants, rise in temperature. Control: smokeless chulha or biogas; chimney filters and factories away from houses; CNG and unleaded petrol; planting trees.

questions.q: Explain how soil gets polluted and suggest five ways to control soil pollution.
questions.answer: Soil is polluted by industrial chemicals and metals, excess pesticides and fertilisers, rotting garbage, and open defecation, urination and spitting, which spread germs and worms; walking barefoot lets them enter the body. Control: (1) dispose of garbage in covered bins and pits; (2) use landfills; (3) compost garden waste; (4) use sanitary latrines; (5) use fewer pesticides and fertilisers; (6) buy Eco-mark products.
